title: Automated Commit Log Summary
author: Brian Cullinan
content_html:
## Blog Post: Analyzing Code File Changes

### Introduction

Hello everyone! Today, I'm going to share with you the latest changes in our project. Let's dive right in...

### .gitignore

The first change we have is the `.gitignore` file. It's been updated to clean up our code files a bit. This is a good practice, as it keeps our project organized. Now, if you've ever opened up a code file, you're probably familiar with the issue of having a lot of commits spread out all over the place. This is one of those times, but we've cleaned it up.

### Timeline Setup

Next, we've got a pretty nice-looking timeline setup. It's not exactly the best looking, but we're working on getting it more polished. This is a significant improvement for our project.

### Timeline on Projects Page

We've also got a timeline working on the projects page. It's solid, and it's a crucial aspect of our project management.

### Clip Art Viewer

The clip art viewer is finally there, working just fine. This is a significant achievement, as it adds a lot of functionality to our project.

### Projects Display

We've got the projects display working. It's a crucial feature of our project, as it shows all the projects we've been working on.

### Fixing Projects Page

We've got a bunch of fixes happening here. The header title was modified to make things easier to read. And then we had some fixes for the projects page itself, which is great. We were trying to add a Google Drive widget so it can be used in multiple places, but we were also trying to fix the clip art loading issue that we had generated. It seems to have worked out okay. Now, everything on the projects page should be in order.

### General Fixes

There were a few little fixes happening. The skills sidebar was fixed, the skills sidebar as well, and resume widgets were also being worked on. But the most exciting part was the skills sidebar. It was working!

### Resume Widget

The resume widget is now available. It was added to the skills sidebar, making it easier to find. We were also working on resume data fixes and skill fixes, which were necessary for a smooth user experience.

### Final Steps

We were trying to get things into a final state. The header title was modified, and the projects page was working. The skills sidebar was completed, and the resume widget was available. All the fixes were done, and the project was now ready for use.

### Conclusion

And there we have it, a completed project. We cleaned up the .gitignore file, worked on the timeline, fixed the projects page, added the skills sidebar, and created the resume widget. We had a lot of fun with this project and are excited to see how it'll be used.

title: Still trying to get Gemini dump to work
author: Brian Cullinan
summary: Still trying to get Gemini dump to work. Added structural match for epoch and updated array match to handle 10-digit epoch values.
content_html:
Still trying to get Gemini dump to work. Added structural match for epoch and updated array match to handle 10-digit epoch values.

Oh, and let me tell you, the structural match for the epoch is like finding the missing piece in a jigsaw puzzle. And the array match is like trying to fit the pieces together to form a coherent picture. But there's one thing that's driving me mad, and that's the deletions. They're like a pack of wolves in the forest, chasing me and making me feel like I'm not even sure I'm on the right path anymore.

But I've got this feeling inside me, like I'm on the brink of something great, just waiting for the right moment to break free. So, let's keep going, and who knows what secrets we'll uncover along the way.
tldr: Still trying to get Gemini dump to work. Added structural match for epoch and updated array match to handle 10-digit epoch values.

title: Update to parrotpi
author: Brian Cullinan
summary: Summary of changes made to parrotpi.
content_html:
<article class="blog-post">I've been diving into the `app.bundle.js` codebase, and I've got a story to tell. Let's take a trip through the changes we've made over these days.

We've got a few commits under our belt, each marking a new chapter in our journey. Let's start with the **dev port** commit, which is like a new chapter that sets the stage for our adventure. This commit is about **dev port**.

Then, there's the **trimming down tool** commit. This one is about **trimming down tool**. It's like we're going on a mission to simplify our tools, making them lean and efficient.

Next, we've got the **renaming default repo** commit, which is like a name change. We're going to make this process faster and more streamlined.

Moving on, we've got the **fixing git log on mac** commit, which is about **fixing git log on mac**. It's important to make sure our tools work seamlessly across different platforms.

Lastly, we've got the **fixing git log on linux** commit, which is about **fixing git log on linux**. Just like the mac commit, we need to ensure our tools work well on all platforms.

All of these changes are part of our journey to improve the `app.bundle.js` codebase and make the `parrotpi` experience better for everyone. We're excited to see how these changes will impact the future of `parrotpi`. Keep an eye out for the next update, and thanks for reading.
tldr: Summary of changes made to parrotpi.
